correctness.rationale: For all integers \(n,N\ge2\), the pathwise identity \(2N-T=X_1+X_n+2Z\) holds without approximation; the pair count \(W\) dominates \(Z\) and \(\mathbb E(W-Z)\le2(n-1)(N)_3/n^3\) by ordered factorial moments. Colored sample-pair indicators have exact means \(1/n\) and \(2(n-1)/n^2\), aggregate \(q=(3n-2)/n^2\), and shared-index joint probability \(s=(9n-10)/n^3\). Arratia–Goldstein–Gordon Theorem 2 (standard total-variation normalization) gives \(2(b_1+b_2)\), with \(b_1=\binom N2(2N-3)q^2\) and \(b_2=\binom N2\,2(N-2)s\); the original-sampling coupling adds \(2N/n+2(n-1)(N)_3/n^3\). This proves the displayed finite joint total-variation bound, which is \(O(N/n+N^3/n^2)\) and tends to zero for \(N=o(n^{2/3})\). Continuity of Poisson laws and their standard central limit theorem establish all three stated regimes. Exact maximum-variation counts follow from independent sets of interior path bins and Stirling surjections. The provided verification script passed 75,160 finite assertions for all \(2\le n\le6\), \(2\le N\le5\); simulations are diagnostic only and do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The sparse null law of the recently introduced order-sensitive histogram statistic is mathematically motivated because its existing exact dynamic program is costly at large sample sizes and its gamma fit is not a sparse limit theorem. The theorem identifies the natural square-root birthday threshold for its discrete variation defect, gives an explicit distribution-level approximation with absolute uniform error, and establishes the surprising asymptotic independence of order-sensitive variation defects and ordinary birthday collisions from the same data. The exact maximum-mass Stirling formula is a natural tail-calibration invariant. It addresses a distinct non-Gaussian occupancy regime, rather than a one-parameter routine increment or a known table recomputation; no claim of a general downstream testing-power theorem is required or made.
